items.title: Nonlinear Landweber iteration with discrepancy stopping

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, Chapter 11
S. Hubmer, E. Sherina, S. Kindermann, and K. Raik, A numerical comparison of some heuristic stopping rules for nonlinear Landweber iteration, §2.1

items.statement:
Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be open, and let $F:U\to Y$ be Fréchet differentiable at every point with a derivative map $F':U\to\mathcal B(X,Y)$ that is continuous in operator norm. This is the real-Hilbert forward-map convention. Assume Countable Choice, so every bounded derivative $F'(x)$ has the Hilbert adjoint $F'(x)^*:Y\to X$ characterized by $\langle F'(x)u,v\rangle_Y=\langle u,F'(x)^*v\rangle_X$.

An **admissible local instance** consists of an initial point $x_0\in U$, a radius $r>0$, an exact solution $x^\dagger\in\overline B_r(x_0):=\{x\in X:\|x-x_0\|_X\le r\}$ with exact datum $y=F(x^\dagger)$, a noise level $\delta\ge0$, noisy datum $y^\delta\in Y$ with $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$, a constant $0\le\eta<1/2$, a discrepancy parameter $\tau>2(1+\eta)/(1-2\eta)$, and a finite update budget $M\in\mathbb N_0$. The closed outer ball $\overline B_{2r}(x_0)$ is contained in $U$; $\|F'(x)\|\le1$ for every $x\in\overline B_{2r}(x_0)$; and the uniform two-point tangential-cone inequality

$$
\|F(x)-F(\widetilde x)-F'(x)(x-\widetilde x)\|_Y\le\eta\|F(x)-F(\widetilde x)\|_Y
$$

holds for every $x,\widetilde x\in\overline B_{2r}(x_0)$. This is the uniform family of the one-basepoint local tangential-cone inequality; the shared constant and pair domain are part of the admissibility hypothesis. The exact solution and the bounds are analysis data and need not be available to the computational loop.

**Inputs:** $F$, $x_0$, $y^\delta$, $\delta$, $\tau$, and $M$ from an admissible local instance.

**Output:** Either `stopped` with an index $k$, iterate $x_k^\delta$, and residual $\|y^\delta-F(x_k^\delta)\|_Y$, or `budget_exhausted` with the last iterate and its residual.

**Procedure:** Set $x_0^\delta:=x_0$. For $k=0,1,\ldots,M$, compute $r_k^\delta:=\|y^\delta-F(x_k^\delta)\|_Y$. If $r_k^\delta\le\tau\delta$, return `stopped` with $(k,x_k^\delta,r_k^\delta)$. If $k=M$, return `budget_exhausted` with $(k,x_k^\delta,r_k^\delta)$. Otherwise set

$$
x_{k+1}^\delta:=x_k^\delta+F'(x_k^\delta)^*(y^\delta-F(x_k^\delta))
$$

and continue at the next index. Each update is evaluated at a current point in $U$, where the derivative and its Hilbert adjoint are defined.

items.title: Nonlinear Landweber Fejér decrease and discrepancy stopping

references.title: Christian Clason, Regularization of Inverse Problems, Chapter 11, Assumption 11.2, Lemma 11.3, and Theorems 11.4–11.6
S. Hubmer, E. Sherina, S. Kindermann, and K. Raik, A numerical comparison of some heuristic stopping rules for nonlinear Landweber iteration, §2.1

items.statement:
Let $X,Y$ be real Hilbert spaces, let $U\subseteq X$ be open, and let $F:U\to Y$ be Fréchet differentiable at every point with $F':U\to\mathcal B(X,Y)$ continuous in operator norm. Fix $x_0\in U$ and $r>0$ such that $\overline B_{2r}(x_0)\subseteq U$, and suppose an exact solution $x^\dagger\in\overline B_r(x_0)$ satisfies $y=F(x^\dagger)$. Assume $\|F'(x)\|\le1$ for every $x\in\overline B_{2r}(x_0)$ and that, for some $0\le\eta<1/2$,

$$
\|F(x)-F(\widetilde x)-F'(x)(x-\widetilde x)\|_Y\le\eta\|F(x)-F(\widetilde x)\|_Y
$$

for every $x,\widetilde x\in\overline B_{2r}(x_0)$. This is a uniform two-point hypothesis with the derivative based at the first point. Assume Countable Choice so that the bounded derivatives have Hilbert adjoints. For $\delta\ge0$ and $y^\delta\in Y$ with $\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta$, set $x_0^\delta=x_0$ and define the ideal Landweber sequence by

$$
x_{n+1}^\delta=x_n^\delta+F'(x_n^\delta)^*(y^\delta-F(x_n^\delta)).
$$

Let $\tau>2(1+\eta)/(1-2\eta)$. For $\delta>0$, let $N(\delta,y^\delta)$ denote the first $n\in\mathbb N_0$ with $\|y^\delta-F(x_n^\delta)\|_Y\le\tau\delta$, if it exists. Put $d_0=\|x_0-x^\dagger\|_X$ and $c_\tau=1-2\eta-2(1+\eta)/\tau>0$. Then the following hold.

1. For every update before the first discrepancy stop, writing $R_n^\delta=\|y^\delta-F(x_n^\delta)\|_Y$, the squared-error estimate is

   $$
   \|x_{n+1}^\delta-x^\dagger\|_X^2-\|x_n^\delta-x^\dagger\|_X^2\le R_n^\delta\bigl(2(1+\eta)\delta-(1-2\eta)R_n^\delta\bigr).
   $$

   In particular, the iterates are Fejér monotone relative to $x^\dagger$ up to the stop: their distance to $x^\dagger$ does not increase. Here Fejér monotonicity means exactly this nonincrease of distance to the stated solution.

2. If $\delta>0$, the first discrepancy index exists and

   $$
   N(\delta,y^\delta)<C\delta^{-2},\qquad C:=1+\frac{d_0^2}{c_\tau\tau^2}.
   $$

   A run of the finite-budget algorithm with budget $M\ge N(\delta,y^\delta)$ returns `stopped` at this first index; if $M<N(\delta,y^\delta)$, it returns `budget_exhausted` at $M$.

3. For exact data ($\delta=0$ and $y^\delta=y$), the ideal sequence is defined for every $n$, satisfies

   $$
   (1-2\eta)\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\|F(x_n)-y\|_Y^2\le d_0^2,
   $$

   and converges strongly to some $\bar x\in\overline B_{2r}(x_0)$ with $F(\bar x)=y$. No finite stopping index is claimed in the exact-data case.

4. For noisy data ($\delta>0$), the ideal stopped iterates converge uniformly over the admissible noise ball to that same exact-data limit:

   $$
   \lim_{\delta\downarrow0}\ \sup_{\|y^\delta-y\|_Y\le\delta}\|x_{N(\delta,y^\delta)}^\delta-\bar x\|_X=0.
   $$

   For finite-budget runs this conclusion concerns outputs only when their budgets reach the first discrepancy indices. The theorem asserts neither a convergence rate nor that $\bar x$ is an $x_0$-minimum-norm solution.

title: Nonlinear Landweber with discrepancy stopping — Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: The initial residual can already meet the discrepancy threshold
items.statement: Take $X=Y=\mathbb R$ with the usual real Hilbert structure, $U=\mathbb R$, $F(x)=x$, $x_0=x^\dagger=0$, $y=F(x^\dagger)=0$, noise level $\delta=1$, noisy datum $y^\delta=1$, discrepancy parameter $\tau>2$, and update budget $M=0$. The local Landweber assumptions hold with any radius $r>0$ and $\eta=0$, and the initial residual is $1\le\tau\delta$. The algorithm therefore returns `stopped` at index zero with iterate $0$ and residual $1$, before consulting the zero update budget.

items.title: Exact-data Landweber can stall without a local tangential-cone condition
items.statement: Exact solvability by itself is enough for exact-data nonlinear Landweber to converge from every initial point; no local tangential-cone or initial-ball hypothesis is needed.

items.title: Exact data can converge without a finite discrepancy stop
items.statement: Take $X=Y=\mathbb R$, $U=\mathbb R$, $F(x)=x/2$, initial point $x_0=1$, exact solution $x^\dagger=0$, exact datum $y=0$, and exact data $y^\delta=y$ with $\delta=0$. The derivative norm is $1/2$ and the uniform TCC holds with $\eta=0$ on every ball. For any $\tau>2$ and any finite update budget $M$, the ideal exact-data iterates are $x_n=(3/4)^n$ and have strictly positive residual at every finite index. They converge to the exact solution, but the zero discrepancy threshold is never met finitely, so the finite-budget algorithm returns `budget_exhausted`.
